newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria sells Iraq 25,000 T wheat, 5,000 T lentils.
newsitem.headline: Syria sells Iraq 25,000 T wheat, 5,000 T lentils.

text.p: Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade (GECPT) has sold Iraq 25,000 tonnes of wheat and 5,000 tonnes of lentils as part of Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, a GECPT spokesman said on Monday.
He said the deal, concluded earlier through direct negotiations with Iraqi officials at a price of $200 per tonne, was approved recently by the U.N.
The sale of 5,000 tonnes of lentils was also approved and shipment would be made in September.

He said the wheat and lentils would be shipped by road through the Syrian-Iraqi border crossing of al-Tanf, which was approved by the U.N. on August 1 as a new entry point for humanitarian goods to Iraq under the oil-for-food plan.

Officials said other food products worth $20 million, agreed through direct negotiations between Syrian and Iraqi traders and which did not require approval of the U.N., would start to flow to Iraq shortly.
They said 10 U.N. inspectors were expected to arrive soon at al-Tanf in Syria, which is opposite the al-Walid entry point in Iraq, to monitor the flow of the goods to Iraq.
Work was still underway to rehabilitate al-Tanf, closed for about 17 years, to enable it to handle the flow of goods. It was expected to be completed by the end of August.

The border between Syria and Iraq, closed since the beginning of 1980 when Syria sided with Iran in its 1980-1988 war with Iraq, was reopened over two months ago after the improvement of Syrian-Iraqi ties.
A high-ranking Iraqi industrial team led by Adnan al-Qudsi, chairman of the Iraqi Industrial Union, is currently in Syria to negotiate the purchase of more Syrian products.
The team met Syrian Minister of Economy and Foreign Trade Mohammed Imadi and Industry Minister Ahmad Nezamuldin to discuss how to boost trade co-operation in line with the oil-for-food deal.
Under the deal Iraq is allowed to export $2 billion worth of oil every six months to help offset the effects of sanctions imposed shortly after its August 2, 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
